Ben / Oliver / Priyom —

I reviewed Brightline's annotated MSA and drafted a compact set of redlines intended to be operationally implementable and acceptable from our risk standpoint. Key points in Redwood's proposed language (attached) are below:

1) Scope and Defense/Control. Redwood will defend and control third-party claims alleging direct infringement (patent, copyright, trademark) arising from the unmodified hosted model outputs ("Model-Origin Claims"). For claims that are attributable to Customer-supplied content, instructions, or material modifications to the model, the Customer will be responsible.

2) Notice; Cooperation; Cure Window. Customer must provide written notice within 30 days of becoming aware of a claim. Redwood must be given reasonable cooperation and sole control of the defense; however, Customer may participate at its own expense. We keep a 30-day cure/cooperation window where parties will exchange technical evidence and attempt remediation to avoid litigation.

3) Escrow / Insurance Offset. Redwood is willing to accept an escrow/insurance-offset mechanism that kicks in when the total paid damages and defense costs exceed $250,000. We propose an explicit mechanics clause: either (a) Redwood will submit claim documentation and insurance determinations and Brightline may draw on escrow previously funded by Redwood's dedicated escrow account up to an agreed cap, or (b) where escrow is not immediately available, an agreed insurance-funds offset shall apply subject to policy limits. We added evidence and timing requirements to prevent spurious draws.

4) Limited Carveouts. Redwood reserves the right to exclude liability where claims arise from: (i) Customer provided data or prompts that infringe third-party rights; (ii) Customer’s deployment of model modifications outside Redwood's managed runtime; or (iii) content explicitly labelled by the Customer as third-party-provided licensed content.

5) SLA Exceptions and Remedy Interaction. If an incident activates the escrow/offset, Redwood also requests a brief SLA exception carveout that allows for investigation (an agreed 14–30 day window) without immediate penalty — we can define escalation metrics in the order form.

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redlines.docx (includes tracked redlines and replacement paragraphs)
